Paul thanks God that the Corinthians lack no spiritual gift. What gifts of grace can you thank God for?
Paul urges them to agree and avoid divisions. What causes division among believers, and how can you help?
The message of the cross looks like folly to the world but is God's power. Why does the cross seem foolish to some?
God chose what is weak and lowly so no one may boast. How does this encourage you?
Paul came in weakness so their faith would rest on God's power. Where does your faith rest?
"What no eye has seen... God has prepared for those who love him." What does this promise stir in you?
Paul says we have the mind of Christ. How can you think more like Christ this week?
Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. How does this free you from pressure or pride?
Each person's work will be tested. What are you building your life on?
You are God's temple and the Spirit dwells in you. How does this change how you see yourself?
Paul says what matters is being found faithful, and the Lord is the judge. How does this free you from others' opinions?
Paul asks, "What do you have that you did not receive?" How does this keep us humble?
Paul urges them to imitate him as a father. Who has shown you how to follow Jesus?
Paul says a little leaven leavens the whole lump. Why does sin we tolerate affect others?
Christ our Passover lamb has been sacrificed. What does this mean for how we live?
Paul distinguishes between judging those in the church and those outside. What does this teach about our posture to the world?
Paul asks why they take each other to court. How should believers handle conflict with one another?
"Such were some of you. But you were washed." What does it mean to you that you are washed?
"You are not your own, for you were bought with a price." How can you glorify God in your body?
Paul speaks of each person having their own gift from God. How can you serve God in your current season of life?
Paul says to lead the life the Lord has assigned you. How can you serve God right where you are?
Paul wants them to have undivided devotion to the Lord. What divides your devotion?
"Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up." How do you balance knowing and loving?
There is one God the Father and one Lord Jesus Christ. What does this mean for your daily choices?
Paul would give up his freedom rather than make a brother stumble. Where might you lay aside a right for someone's sake?
Paul had rights as an apostle but did not use them. Why did he give them up?
Paul became all things to all people that he might save some. How can you meet people where they are?
Paul says to run so as to obtain the prize. What discipline helps you in the race of faith?
These things happened as examples for us. What lesson from Israel's story do you need?
God will provide a way of escape in temptation. What way out has God given you?
Paul says flee from idolatry. What might be an idol in your life today?
"Whatever you do, do all to the glory of God." What everyday task can you do for God's glory today?
"Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ." Who can you imitate, and who might be imitating you?
Paul rebuked them because the rich ate while the poor went hungry. How can the church care for all its members?
Jesus said, "Do this in remembrance of me." What do you remember at the Lord's Supper?
Paul says to examine yourself. What might God want you to set right?
There are varieties of gifts but the same Spirit. What gifts have you seen the Spirit give in your church?
The body has many parts but is one. Which part do you think you are?
If one member suffers, all suffer together. Who in your church is suffering that you can support?
You are the body of Christ. How does this shape how you see your fellowship?
Without love, even great gifts are nothing. Why is love so central?
Read these verses putting your name in place of "love." Which line is hardest for you?
"Faith, hope, and love abide; but the greatest of these is love." Why is love the greatest?
Paul wants gifts used to build up the church. How can you build others up?
"Strive to excel in building up the church." What could that look like for you?
"Let all things be done for building up," and God is a God of peace. How can our gatherings reflect that?
Paul passes on what is of first importance: Christ died, was buried and was raised. Why do these facts matter so much?
Paul says, "By the grace of God I am what I am." How has grace shaped who you are?
Paul says if Christ is not raised our faith is futile. Why does everything rest on the resurrection?
Paul compares the resurrection body to a seed. What does this teach about our future hope?
"Death is swallowed up in victory." How does this change how you face death and do your work?
Paul asks each to set aside something on the first day of the week. How do you plan your giving?
"Be watchful, stand firm, act like men, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love." Which do you need most?
Paul honours those who devoted themselves to serving the saints. Who could you thank for serving?
